projects.title: Coffee rater app
projects.description:
February 13, 2026

Just bought 8 new types of coffees and I want to make sure I remember which one I like best. But also in the future, I'll likely keep trying other brands, so having a rater app will be cool.

For this one, I'm going to build on top of the liquor rater I've already created. I'm not really happy with the interface, but improving that won't be my focus for this project.

What I want to achieve here is something I've never tried before, so I want to really focus on that. This app needs to include three additional things that the liquor rater doesn't:
• A chat interface to help me determine the flavour profile and my rating
• At least two user accounts
• A social feed to see the ratings of other users

 Total Implementation:
• Files Created: 50+ (components, pages, routes, utilities)
• Lines of Code: ~5,000+
• Features: 25+ major features
• Documentation: 4 comprehensive guides
• Cost of around 17 dollars before testing

---

February 15, 2026

Claude wrote the documentation for deployment and I double-checked some things in Le Chat. They seem to agree on the next steps, so I'll try to implement it that way today.

But first some local testing, I thought. Turns out I can't test without a database so I'll connect and deploy to railway right away.

As usual, after an hour of back-and-forthing I'm still not there. Making progress? Yes. But some dependencies were outdated and god knows what else is wrong. Even got to a stage where Claude is using me as a human to update files manually. Who would've thought?

And another two hours of debugging in the evening. Claude doesn't seem to have all the latest info and it's actually contradicting what Railway says. Claude thinks Railpack is outdated but it's actually Nixpacks that's deprecated. 

Perhaps the long context window wasn't helping. After compacting the context, Claude suggested more elaborate changes.

Found the issue: Claude told me to write port 3000 in the settings for my custom domain but the app was listening to port 8080. Had to find it on my own. Still wasted lots of credits and two hours of my time, but does this now mean I'm smarter than Claude? lol.

Short-lasting sense of victory. Can't even create an account. It was a parsing issue. But also the username can't have @ but the label says username or email. Nice one, Claude. 

I'll fix those manually later. It's almost working now. Just an authentication issue because the cookie is missing (says Claude). To be fixed by adding another variable: CLIENT_URL

PS: If you've read it this far, you can test the app via coffee.kjellv.com - enjoy. (but it's in Spanish)

---

February 16, 2026

Finally fixed the cookie issue. Just in time, because I'm down to the last coffee of this batch.

Never mind, saving a coffee still doesn't work. Small user-id issue. Claude says "The schema was expecting userId in the request body, but it should come from the authenticated user (req.user.id), not from the client. I've added userId to the omit list."

Up and running now :)

projects.title: Finance tracking
projects.description:
February 9, 2026

I just realised that I don't have a solid view of my business expenses. I know that I typically earn more than I spend, but how much?
No better way to find out, than to vibe code a desktop app to keep track of invoices sent and received. 
Initially, it doesn't need to be complicated. The only tricky part is the difference between one-off expenses, and monthly, quarterly and yearly recurring ones. 

When this part works, I also want to develop a personal tracker. I've been tracking my investments in a Number sheet for over 10 years and it's getting kind of clunky. I'm also pretty sure there are some mistakes in my logic. So I can fix it and add it to my tracker.

Later on, if everything works, I could look at automating parts. I'm especially thinking about syncing expenses. Open banking is something I'm not going to get involved with, though.

This session, Claude generated:
• 26 Swift files (~3,700 lines of code)
• 24 source files
• 2 test files (30+ unit tests)
• 6 documentation files (comprehensive guides)
• 100% of planned features implemented

This version included an App with CloudKit. It sounded like an overkill for an app that just needs to sync between my devices, but what do I know? Only after trying to set it up in Xcode, my suspicions were confirmed.

It cost less than $5 so far. But it will probably end up costing a lot more as I need quite some back and forth to roll back Cloud capabilities that aren't available to free plans. Easily spent an extra hour on this as well. 

Damn, it looks like a real Apple App. Not what I expected but pretty nice apart from some alignment issues.

---

February 10, 2026

After some further back and forth, I got the app to work with decent padding too.

Now, I'm most definitely not going to use the same app for personal finances because it's going to break again. But I can use the structure and learnings from this to create another one.

Only thing left to do now is figure out how i can add this app to my desktop and how to give it a logo so I don't have to run it from Xcode every time.

### next changes
• net profit = difference between income and expenses without VAT
• (later include more detailed calcs for VAT based on category)
• Save names of expenses eg charging
• Detailed overview of expenses per name instead of category
• quarterly and yearly costs -> split over months

projects.title: Rent scraper
projects.description:
February 5, 2026

We're looking for larger place to live but there aren't many larger houses for rent.
It's getting quite tiring to check 10+ real estate pages from time to time, so would be great if I could make a scraper that pulls in new houses for rent that match my requirements.

Just planning with Claude Code cost a surprising lot of tokens. It took around 250k tokens just to analyse previous projects and find parts to re-use. I wonder if that was worth the effort. At least, it did come up with a very detailed and well-structured plan.

While fine-tuning the plan it helped to stop and clarify that I'm looking for a simple solution. That made Claude suggest to create an email digest instead of an app.

First result looks pretty nice - however the scrapers don't work well. Only 13 listings were found from the first three implemented websites. 2 passed the filters but they didn't actually meet the requirements that we set at the start.

To get all the listings, Claude had to create scrapers for every page. It took two tries for most websites but five out of fourteen didn't work according to Claude. I asked what I could do manually, but the suggestions were and API or installing more complicated dependencies. Instead, I inspected a page and copied the exact path to where the room numbers is on the page. This helped me fix one scraper. On to the next now.

projects.title: Liquor rater
projects.description:
February 3, 2026

There's Vivino for wines and Untappd for beers but what about liquors?
Don't judge me.
I received a set of about 20 whisky and rhum samples. And I also got 12 last year. They're only 2cl each but I want a place to track and rate them.

Claude Code very quickly created an HMTL file that basically does everything. It seemed functional, but no separate style sheet and no separate database sound wrong to me.

Claude split it up into a js server, json files for data and css style sheet. Still looks the same. Impressive. 

Currently no public repo, might push it later if it looks better.

Separating tabs for collection and adding a new entry really made it look better.

---

February 4, 2026

Tried to implement voice transcription as well last night, but that didn't seem to work because it needs internet access and this is a local app (for now).
So I'm going to include OCR instead to speed up text input. That seems to work better.
I'm also making some changes to the layout and card field: adding years of aging and putting it in two columns so it stays in one screen.

projects.title: Vibing tracker
projects.description:
January 29, 2026

Tried to deploy the Vibe coding Activity Tracker online by setting up GitHub Pages with automatic deployment and configured local SiteGround deployment via SFTP.                              

Unfortunately, Siteground wasn't really working along as the files could not be pushed.

At some point I managed to show my page successfully on vibing.kjellv.com but without actually showing my activity.

Almost there but not quite yet.

---

January 30, 2026

I gave up trying to push the files directly to Siteground. 
With a CNAME record, however, my github page now gets shown on vibing.kjellv.com
This requires a workflow in github that Claude wrote.

Additionally, i added a cron job to parse my Obsidian files daily and push the changes to github so that my activity tracker gets updated daily (when I'm online)

Finally, I added a button in the header to go back to kjellv.com. Believe it or not, I coded this manually with some HTML and CSS. At least I have the feeling that I contributed a bit now.

---

February 4, 2026

Made some small changes to how projects and days are being parsed.
One project per note file: Each Obsidian note is now treated as a single project, regardless of how many date sections (H2 headers) it contains. 
Chronological ordering: Date sections within a note are now sorted chronologically (oldest to newest) before being processed and aggregated.
Aggregated content: All work sessions from different dates are combined into a single project entry with:
• The earliest date as the main project date
• All content from all sessions aggregated
• All learnings combined
• Maximum intensity across all sessions
• A new workDates array that tracks all the dates you worked on that project
Clean titles: Project titles no longer have "(Day 1)", "(Day 2)" labels.

---

February 5, 2026

The changes from yesterday didn't really work out the way I wanted.
I trusted Claude to just change everything at once but it didn't work.
I then tried again, giving more and clearer instructions but it almost reversed the changes instead.
Today, I tried implementing the small changes one by one, instead.
The key learning here is that you can't ask too much at once. I actually knew this from the very first time I started vibe coding but i was starting to trust the machine too much.

projects.title: Sally, customer success oracle
projects.description:
January 28, 2026

Just made a Slack bot that everyone in the team can talk to to ask questions about our successful customers. 

But it can also answer other questions like: 
• Which customers are in IT? 
• Which customers have an office manager? 
• Who had the most impressions last year? 

How does it work? 

Two simple n8n workflows. 
Every time a new success story gets added (or updated) to Webflow, it gets synced to a database 
Slack messages get passed on to an AI Agent who only takes the database as a single source of truth. The reply gets sent back to the same slack channel.

---

January 29, 2026

Sally lives on ww.willow.co/success-stories too now.
Been wanting to implement this for months but never felt confident about how to do it.
Since I got more experience with webhooks now, I gave it another shot and it was easier than expected.
Starting with a script for Webflow written by ChatGPT, it was easy enough to connect it to n8n and send back replies to the web page. 
Styling it was something I could easily do manually as well.
Pretty happy with the result.

projects.title: Wardrobe
projects.description:
January 16, 2026

First time working with Claude Code. Developed fully locally.
Learning here is that the main file is definitely too large. 
Wondering why CSS isn't separated for example.
Also the stack was too light to make it work visually, but again maybe it's related to the CSS too.
Good but expensive learning experience (around 28$)

---

January 27, 2026
Converted desktop app to web app - Transformed the CustomTkinter desktop wardrobe manager into a Flask-based web application
Unified database - Merged separate wardrobe.db and wardrobe_fer.db into single database with `wardrobe` field to distinguish owners
Added search & filter - Implemented debounced search (300ms), type filtering, and sorting by rating/brand/date
Built REST API - Created 10+ Flask endpoints for CRUD operations, search, filter, sort, and undo functionality
Vanilla JS frontend - Developed SPA with state management, API client, and modular components (ItemCard, ItemModal, SearchFilter)
CSS theme system - Implemented CSS variables for instant theme switching between Kjell's earthy and Fer's pink color schemes
Preserved features - Maintained all original functionality: color-coded cards, 10-star ratings, color picker, edit/delete with undo
Migrated 72 items - Successfully transferred all items from Kjell's wardrobe with full data integrity and backups
Responsive design - Built mobile-friendly grid layout with auto-fill columns and media queries for various screen sizes
Complete documentation - Created README, INSTALL, QUICKSTART guides plus verification scripts for easy setup and troubleshooting

Key Features
• View items organized by clothing type
• Add/edit/delete items with confirmation
• Color-coded item cards with contrast text
• 10-star rating system
• Color picker for custom colors
• Switch between Kjell's and Fer's wardrobes
• Undo delete (10-second window)
• Automatic data persistence
• Search - Full-text search across brand, model, materials with debouncing
• Filter - Dropdown to filter by specific clothing type
• Sort - Multiple sort options (rating desc, brand asc, date desc)
• Responsive - Mobile-friendly grid layout
• Keyboard shortcuts - ESC to close modals
• Real-time updates - Observer pattern for reactive UI
• API access - RESTful endpoints for external integration

Access at: http://localhost:5001 (changed from 5000 to avoid macOS AirPlay conflict)
